indexes._comment: Requests are queried by denormalised membership so the query matches what firestore.rules authorises (uid in allParticipantIDs). An OR over creatorID/recipientIDs is denied for list queries because Firestore cannot prove every match is readable.
FirestoreRelationshipRepository.fetchRelationships filters by membership and orders by createdAt.

CloudFunctions pendingCountFor() — the push badge counts every unsettled request this user belongs to, then narrows to the ones awaiting their reply in JS. Membership is `allParticipantIDs`, not `recipientIDs`: after a counter-offer the turn belongs to the creator, who is in neither the recipients nor a `pending` status.

weeklyNudge in CloudFunctions reads a user's plans newest-first to find which group has gone longest without one. Ordering by `proposedTime` also does the filtering: undated requests lack the field and Firestore omits them, which is correct — a chore is not a plan.
promptForAttendance in CloudFunctions finds accepted plans whose time fell inside one hourly window — an equality on `status` plus a range on `proposedTime`.

dailyDigest in CloudFunctions counts each event type over a 24h window — an equality on `type` plus a range on `at`. Without this the aggregation fails FAILED_PRECONDITION and the digest reports '?' for every row rather than erroring visibly.

FirestoreEventRepository.events(forUser:) — equality on userID plus an order on `at` needs a composite index. Without it the query fails FAILED_PRECONDITION, and AdminViewModel swallows that in a `try?`, so the admin Activity section silently reported 'No events recorded' instead of erroring.

fieldOverrides._comment: Shared locations are deleted rather than kept. TTL is what makes 'it expires with the plan' true on the server instead of only in the client's filter — without it a coordinate written for one evening sits in Firestore indefinitely, which is not what the App Privacy answers say. Firestore promises deletion within 24 hours of `expiresAt`, not at the instant, so FirestoreSharedLocationRepository also filters lapsed points on read.

Usage events are written on every user action and are never read after the reporting window, so without a TTL the collection grows without bound while carrying personal data indefinitely. Firestore deletes each document 90 days after its `at` value. Requires Blaze — under Spark this returns HTTP 403 and fails the whole firestore deploy. The 90-day retention sentence in docs/legal/privacy-policy.md must stay in step with this.
